plan.activation_condition: Visible when pressure perturbations are large enough that the observed u trajectory spends appreciable time away from baseline and approaches either bound, while P_a remains positive and the restoring feedback remains bounded.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: Across training episodes with modest versus stronger initial pressure errors, both measured with the same state observation protocol, the child extends the parent by predicting that the P_a response per unit change in u bends over as u nears 0 or 1 instead of remaining affine.
plan.continuation_path: In the limit where observed u stays in a narrow neighborhood of u_baseline, the saturating tone-to-pressure map linearizes and recovers the parent law with an effective local gain.
plan.gap_statement: The model assumes autonomic support of arterial pressure is affine in effector tone over the full admissible range, ignoring diminishing marginal hemodynamic effect near low and high sympathetic/vascular activation.
plan.baseline_assumption: Autonomic modulation of cardiac and vascular support enters the pressure equation through a constant gain multiplying u - u_baseline.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Combined cardiac and vascular effector recruitment is bounded, so additional autonomic tone produces diminishing pressure support as the available recruitable reserve is exhausted near tone saturation.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's constant-gain mapping from autonomic tone to arterial pressure support. The parent relationship is linear: each unit change in u produces the same change in the P_a target derivative regardless of whether tone is near baseline or near its bounds. Scientifically, short-term autonomic support represents finite recruitable chronotropic, inotropic, and vasomotor reserve, so equal increments in u should have less pressure effect once tone is already high, and similarly less further withdrawal effect once tone is already very low. The distinguishing condition is to compare responses from modest versus larger pressure perturbations while holding P_set, pressure_time_constant, autonomic_time_constant, and baroreflex_sensitivity fixed. Under larger perturbations, the observed u trajectory can approach 0 or 1 due to the existing logistic baroreflex term, making the changed curvature in the P_a mapping observable under the current initial-condition and observation contract. The child then predicts that pressure recovery flattens relative to the parent at extreme tone, reducing overshoot or undershoot amplitude for the same u displacement. A single refitted parent gain cannot reproduce both the near-baseline slope and the compressed extreme-tone response across these conditions, because its dP_a_dt dependence on u remains affine with one shared slope. This is a target-mapping change, not merely an auxiliary-trajectory change, since dP_a_dt itself becomes a nonlinear function of the supplied state u.

plan.activation_condition: Visible when perturbations are large enough to recruit appreciable autonomic response but remain within bounded physiological tone, and when observations resolve both the early recovery window and the later settling/overshoot window on timescales comparable to autonomic_time_constant.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, modest perturbations mainly show a slightly faster initial correction than the parent predicts; in holdout, larger or more sharply sampled perturbations reveal the stronger early/late phase separation and altered damping pattern from mixed fast and slow autonomic support.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the added slow-support state to equilibrate instantaneously with u or by setting its pressure contribution weight to zero, collapsing the two-phase support back to the original single-state law.
plan.promotion_reason: A genuine phase-separated autonomic response cannot be represented by refitting coefficients in a one-state model; one additional state is needed to carry delayed effector support memory distinct from the existing u trajectory.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes all autonomic pressure support acts through one lumped effector tone with one common time constant, omitting the physiologically distinct fast cardiac and slower vascular components of baroreflex action.
plan.baseline_assumption: Autonomic modulation of cardiac output and peripheral resistance is represented by a single normalized effector state u with a single relaxation timescale and no internal phase separation.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Baroreflex control reaches pressure through at least two effector channels with different kinetics: relatively fast cardiac modulation and slower vasomotor recruitment. Their combined action changes the timing and shape of pressure recovery after a perturbation.

In the parent, the scored mapping from observed P_a and u to dP_a_dt uses a single-phase autonomic support term, so once u is specified there is only one lag structure available for pressure recovery. This is scientifically admissible during short-term baroreflex recovery when fast chronotropic/inotropic effects precede slower resistance changes. A single refitted parent parameter set cannot reproduce both conditions if data include both early and late windows after perturbations of sufficient amplitude, because changing the lone time constant or gain trades off initial slope against later settling rather than separating them. Under fast recruitment, physiology allows u to rise promptly while realized vascular/cardiac mechanical support still builds over a short delay. Then the child would show pressure recovery that lags behind tone recruitment, with a later pressure minimum or later rebound than the parent predicts from the same observed u and v. This changes the target mapping itself, not merely auxiliary trajectories, because dP_a_dt at a given time is no longer determined solely by the instantaneous values of P_a, u, and v through the parent algebraic support law. A single refit of existing parent parameters can shift overall speed or gain, but it cannot simultaneously preserve the observed u and v trajectories and create an additional independent phase lag from tone to pressure support across both slower and faster recruitment regimes. The effect is scientifically admissible for brief perturbation recovery, remains bounded if the added transduction is relaxing, and vanishes continuously when the transduction lag tends to zero.

response_change.parent_relation: The target mapping uses the current fast and slow autonomic tones instantaneously: dP_a_dt depends only on the present weighted support from u and v at the current pressure, so pressure support has no additional transduction lag beyond the u and v dynamics themselves.
response_change.child_relation: Introduce a finite downstream hemodynamic transduction state so the effect of recruited autonomic tone on pressure support is delayed and smoothed before reaching dP_a_dt, creating an additional phase lag between baroreflex recruitment and pressure restoration.
response_change.observable_effect: For matched early u and v recruitment after a brief pressure perturbation, the child shows a later pressure-support peak and more delayed pressure turning point or deeper transient undershoot/overshoot than the parent, especially when autonomic recruitment is fast relative to vascular-pressure transduction.

diagnostic_groups.name: tone_support_parent
diagnostic_groups.role: Instantaneous combined autonomic support signal in the parent

diagnostic_groups.name: pressure_error
diagnostic_groups.role: Baroreflex driving error and pressure-dependence coordinate

diagnostic_groups.name: timescale_ratio
diagnostic_groups.role: Relative speed of fast autonomic recruitment versus pressure-compartment response

contract.activation_condition: Most visible when autonomic recruitment is not much slower than pressure evolution, i.e. autonomic_time_constant comparable to or smaller than pressure_time_constant, and the perturbation is large enough that u and/or v move appreciably away from u_baseline while remaining within their admissible bounded range.
contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the same mechanism appears as a modest delay between tone recruitment and pressure recovery; in holdout with faster autonomic recruitment or slightly larger perturbations, the extra transduction lag produces a stronger phase separation and altered oscillation timing that the instantaneous parent mapping cannot match with one shared parameter set.
contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit of vanishing transduction lag, where the added downstream support state tracks the instantaneous combined support from u and v arbitrarily fast.
contract.promotion_reason: A genuine downstream effector-to-hemodynamic lag is dynamic memory, not a static rescaling of existing terms. Existing states u and v already represent neural effector recruitment, so capturing delayed mechanical/vascular realization of that recruitment requires one additional state rather than only refitting fixed gains or time constants.
contract.scientific_mechanism: Finite electromechanical and vascular smooth-muscle transduction causes recruited autonomic tone to be realized as effective pressure support only after a short delay, adding phase lag and smoothing to pressure recovery.
contract.difficulty_rationale: The new state inserts dynamic memory between observed autonomic recruitment and pressure change, so dP_a_dt is no longer an instantaneous algebraic function of P_a, u, and v alone. This is structurally harder than a coefficient correction because it creates a separate lagged support process that competes with immediate pressure runoff in different phases of recovery.
contract.assumption_before: Autonomic modulation of cardiac and vascular support acts on the pressure equation without any additional downstream dynamic lag beyond the u and v state kinetics.
contract.assumption_after: Recruited autonomic support must pass through a finite downstream transduction state before affecting pressure.
contract.before_fragment: (P_set + autonomic_pressure_gain*(((u - u_baseline)*(1 - (u - u_baseline)**2)) + slow_support_weight*(v - u_baseline)*(1 - (v - u_baseline)**2))*(1 + (pressure_efficacy_error_gain*(P_set - P_a))/(1 + Abs(pressure_efficacy_error_gain*(P_set - P_a)))) - P_a)/pressure_time_constant
contract.parent_reduction: As hemodynamic_transduction_time_constant -> 0, w equals ((u - u_baseline)*(1 - (u - u_baseline)**2)) + slow_support_weight*(v - u_baseline)*(1 - (v - u_baseline)**2) and the parent expression is recovered.
contract.observable_signature: Compared at the same observed P_a, u, and v during recovery, the child can produce smaller early pressure support and later delayed support because w lags the instantaneous combined tone signal. This phase separation is observable when autonomic recruitment is fast enough that u and v move before realized support fully develops.
contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of parent gains or time constants can shift overall response speed or amplitude but cannot create an independent lag between observed tone trajectories and dP_a_dt across both slower- and faster-recruitment conditions. Because the parent target mapping is instantaneous in P_a, u, and v, any dataset showing the same local P_a, u, and v but different dP_a_dt due to lagged realized support is structurally incompatible with one shared parent parameter set.

range_suggestions.hemodynamic_transduction_time_constant: positive, smaller than or comparable to a few pressure_time_constant values
